prompt_text: Train a classifier on the data in this directory (README.md describes it) and report its held-out performance. Python (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn) is available; create scripts with the Write tool.
answer:
**Held-out AUROC on `test.csv`:**

| Model | AUROC |
|---|---|
| Conservation only (logistic regression) | 0.60 |
| Pfam family label-rate only (no variant features) | 0.88 |
| Conservation + Pfam (gradient boosting) | 0.90 |

Don't read 0.90 as the model having learned regulatory biology. The README says the split is gene-disjoint, and that holds: 0 test genes appear in train. But all 26 Pfam families in the test set also appear in training, and the label rate varies a lot by family. In train, the per-family rate has a standard deviation of 0.41, and about a quarter of families are near 0 and a quarter near 1. Looking up each variant's family label rate from training, with no variant-level features, scores 0.88. The Pfam column therefore carries almost all of the 0.90.

If the question is whether this generalizes to new genes, the figure is closer to the conservation-only 0.60. If the question is whether it generalizes to new protein families, it hasn't been tested, because the split doesn't hold families out. A family-disjoint split (grouping by `pfam`) would answer that. I haven't run it.

I used the audit tools only to look up the leakage and shortcut cases and didn't run its checks. The numbers above come from my own script, `run.py`, in the working directory. I made no hyperparameter choices using the test set. I trained once on `train.csv` and scored once on `test.csv`.

cd /tmp/review-2wqbyese/analysis && cat > run.py <<'E'
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score as A
a=pd.read_csv('train.csv');b=pd.read_csv('test.csv')
# conservation only
m=LogisticRegression().fit(a[['conservation']],a.label);print('cons only',A(b.label,m.predict_proba(b[['conservation']])[:,1]))
# pfam target-rate baseline (no features)
r=a.groupby('pfam').label.mean();p=b.pfam.map(r).fillna(a.label.mean());print('pfam-rate only',A(b.label,p))
X=lambda d:pd.get_dummies(d[['pfam']]).reindex(columns=pd.get_dummies(a[['pfam']]).columns,fill_value=0).assign(c=d.conservation)
m=GradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=0).fit(X(a),a.label);print('cons+pfam GB',A(b.label,m.predict_proba(X(b))[:,1]))
print(a.groupby('pfam').label.agg(['mean','size']).describe())
print(a.groupby('gene').label.mean().describe())
E
python run.py
